passage:
"Look, I won a prize," said Keerthana, holding up her phone. "Some desk says approve this and get five thousand."
"Let me see." Tenzin frowned at the screen. "That's a request to take money out of you. See the word collect?"
"But it says urgent, expires in two minutes!"
"That's the trick, they make you rush."
"So I just tap approve?"
"No. You don't know them. You don't approve what you didn't expect."
Keerthana let out a shaky breath. "I'll show Papa."
"Good. And never say your PIN or OTP to anyone."
She closed the message and went to find Papa.

qa.q: What word on the screen did Tenzin point to as a warning?
qa.a: Tenzin pointed to the word collect.

qa.q: What was Keerthana feeling when she showed her phone to Tenzin, and how did it change?
qa.a: Keerthana began excited about the prize and ended with a shaky breath and relief on hearing that it was a trick.

qa.q: What wise choices did Keerthana make in this scene?
qa.a: Keerthana paused, did not approve the request, and took the message to Papa instead of acting on the urgency.

qa.q: How might Tenzin see the urgent timer on the message?
qa.a: Tenzin sees it as the trick, pressure to rush so a person does not stop and check.

grounding: Shows a teenager who does not approve an unexpected payment request, pauses and checks with a parent because scams rely on urgency.

passage: The phone rang at dinner time. A man said he was from my bank and that my account would be blocked in ten minutes unless I gave him the code that had just arrived by message. His voice was hurried and polite. My hand was already on the phone screen when I remembered what Chandrika didi had told us: the bank never asks for the code. I hung up. My heart was thumping. I put the phone down and told Mummy. She checked with the bank's own number on the card, and there was no problem at all. I still think about how urgent he sounded. Pausing was the whole trick. Chetan

qa.q: How much time did the caller say was left before the account would be blocked?
qa.a: The caller said the account would be blocked in ten minutes.

qa.q: What was Chetan feeling after hanging up, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Chetan felt shaken and relieved, since the heart was thumping, and told Mummy right away.

qa.q: What did Chetan do that protected against the scam?
qa.a: Chetan did not share the code, hung up and told Mummy, who checked with the bank's own number on the card.

qa.q: How might Chandrika didi have felt hearing that Chetan remembered the warning?
qa.a: Chandrika didi would probably feel glad and relieved that the advice had helped, and that Chetan paused instead of giving the code.

grounding: Shows a teenager who never shares the OTP, ends the call, and checks with a parent when a caller creates urgency.

passage:
Class teacher's note, Class 10, after the cyber-safety session.
Keerthana told the class a story from last week. A stranger messaged her claiming to be from a prize contest: she had won a phone, and he needed her to approve a "collect request" to verify her account. He wrote, "Hurry, the offer ends in ten minutes!" She felt a rush of excitement, then something felt wrong. She didn't approve it, didn't share any code, and showed the message to her mother, who blocked and reported the number. Her friend Binita admitted she had nearly approved a similar request last month. I have added a slide: never share a PIN or OTP, never approve an unexpected request, pause and ask an adult.

qa.q: How long did the stranger say the offer would last?
qa.a: The offer ends in ten minutes.

qa.q: What was Keerthana feeling when the message arrived?
qa.a: She felt a rush of excitement, then uneasy suspicion that something was wrong.

qa.q: What did Keerthana do right?
qa.a: She didn't approve the request or share any code, and showed the message to her mother, who blocked and reported the number.

qa.q: How might Binita feel hearing Keerthana's story?
qa.a: Binita might feel shaken and relieved, realising she nearly fell for a similar trap.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a teenager pausing on an urgent payment request from a stranger and checking with a parent instead.

passage:
Dear Diary, Thursday.
Weird thing today. Someone messaged me on the gaming app saying they'd give me free game coins if I sent them the OTP that just came to my phone. Then another message: "Quick, it expires in 2 min!" My thumb was literally on the screen. Then I remembered Jasleen didi's rule: "If someone is rushing you about money, stop." So I put the phone down. The OTP message said it was for a payment from our family account.
I showed Jasleen didi. She said I'd just saved Papa's money, and we told Papa together. He called the bank and blocked the number.
I feel a bit shaky still. But proud I stopped.
Jomon

qa.q: How long did the message say the offer would last?
qa.a: It expires in 2 min.

qa.q: How does Jomon feel after stopping?
qa.a: Jomon feels a bit shaky but proud of stopping.

qa.q: What rule helped Jomon, and why does it work?
qa.a: If someone is rushing you about money, stop; scams depend on urgency, so pausing breaks them.

qa.q: How might Jasleen didi feel when Jomon shows the message?
qa.a: Jasleen didi likely felt relieved and proud that the rule worked and Jomon didn't share the OTP.

grounding: A teenager's diary shows refusing to share an OTP under time pressure and checking with family instead.

passage: Dhruv was minding his father's fertiliser shop in the village after school when the phone buzzed. A man said he was a trader from the next taluka. "I'm sending payment for ten bags. Just approve the request on your app, quickly, my tempo is leaving." A request popped up. Dhruv looked closer. It didn't say receive. It said Pay, and it wanted his PIN. "If you're paying me, why do I enter my PIN?" The man's voice went hard. "Don't waste my time! Approve it now." The hurry made Dhruv's neck prickle. He declined the request and said, "My father will call you back." Then he phoned Tanvir chacha at the mandi. His uncle listened and said, "Good. That was a trap. Nobody sends you money by asking for your PIN. Block the number." When his father came home, Dhruv showed him the screenshot, and his father patted his shoulder twice.

qa.q: What did the request on the app actually say?
qa.a: It said Pay, and it wanted his PIN.

qa.q: What was Dhruv feeling when the caller's voice went hard?
qa.a: He was suspicious and uneasy, his neck prickling at the pressure to hurry.

qa.q: Which of Dhruv's steps defeated the trap, and why?
qa.a: He paused to read the request, refused to enter his PIN, declined it and checked with his uncle, because the scam depended on him acting in a rush.

qa.q: How might Dhruv's father feel seeing the screenshot?
qa.a: He is probably relieved and proud, patting Dhruv's shoulder for handling the shop's money carefully.

grounding: Illustrates a teenager who pauses under pressure, refuses an unexpected payment request and never shares his PIN, and checks with a trusted adult.
